How the dashboard and automatic recovery work.
Connection dashboard: per-account status, history and recovery.
Recover now: full DHT + re-register + presence refresh.

Connection mode: the shape is the mode (filled = full DHT, hollow = DHT proxy); the colour is the state (yellow = receiving fine, blue = switching/recovering/streaming fallback, red = current mode verified broken). Tap to switch — it sets every account at once.
Inbound test: silently re-requests presence on every account and waits 60 s for any real answer from the network — your contacts see nothing. No answer = reception is likely wedged.
Inbound test running — waiting up to %d s for a live answer…
No live answer in %1$d s. If your contacts should be online, reception is likely wedged — run Recover. (If everyone is offline, silence is normal.)

Disconnected — an account is silent, or the network is down
Off — the account is switched off, not trying to connect
No ring: the colour alone shows the state.

You rarely need to touch anything here — a watcher runs continuously and repairs the connection on its own (see \"How auto-recovery works\" below). These controls are for when you want to force a repair yourself.

● Account dot — tap to open this dashboard. Its colour is the connection state: yellow = connected and healthy; blue = connecting or recovering; red = disconnected, an account gone silent, or the network down (it should be up but isn\'t). A hollow dot is different — it means the account is switched off / logged out and is not trying to connect. There is no ring; the dot\'s colour alone shows the state.
⚡ Flash — tap for Recover now: drop to the full DHT, re-register every account and refresh presence. The one strong manual fix; it turns blue while recovering.
Full DHT — robust; no single proxy link that can wedge
Proxy — lighter; inbound rides a proxy server

⬡ Connection-mode icon — its SHAPE is the current mode: filled hub = full DHT (the heavy mode, your device is a node), thick outline = DHT proxy (the light mode). Its COLOUR is the state: yellow = the chosen mode is receiving fine, blue = transitional (post-switch verification, recovery, or the streaming fallback while the push leg is dead), red = the current mode is verifiably not receiving. Tap to switch modes; it sets every account at once, so the per-account “Use DHT proxy” never drifts out of sync.

Account rows — tap a row to expand its contacts and their live connections (connecting → ICE → TLS → connected). Each row has its own ⚡ that recovers just that account, leaving the healthy ones untouched.
⚡ Recover now — the same strong fix as the main-screen flash, for all accounts.

Inbound test (top of the dashboard) — silently checks that the network still answers you: presence is re-requested and any real answer within 60 s counts. It opens a window that streams the watchdog log live from the moment the test starts until the verdict, so you can watch it happen. Use it when you suspect “maybe nothing is reaching me”; no answer offers Recover.
Monitor — opens the full connection monitor for the deepest per-device detail.
Long-press any button, row or icon (here or on the main screen) to see a description of what it does.
A watcher checks the connection about once a minute — and within seconds of trouble. It judges each account by whether real traffic is still arriving, not just by whether it reports \"connected\".

Error storms: a burst of connection failures is only a hint. The watcher recovers on it only when the trouble is confirmed — the network genuinely unreachable, or a message stuck to a contact who is reachable. A burst while the network is fine, or right after a recovery (its own reconnection noise), is ignored. A confirmed problem a first recovery doesn\'t fix escalates to a full reset.

Silent account: silence alone is never acted on. If nothing real arrives for a while, the watcher first checks that the network itself is reachable, then re-requests presence as a silent probe and waits for the verdict — and a delivered push also counts as proof that the receive path is alive. Only an account that stays silent through the probe on a working network is treated as wedged. Quiet is not broken.
Cold start: if accounts don\'t come online within about a minute of launch, it drops straight to the full DHT to connect fast.
Hostile network: if a recovery fails and the network blocks UDP (some hotel / office Wi-Fi), it pins the proxy ON and relays over TCP, re-testing every 2 minutes and switching back when UDP returns.
Stuck messages: an undelivered message to an offline contact is ignored (that\'s their side); only a message stuck to a contact who is reachable counts as a problem.
Off because the phone is charging — the search-bar hexagon still says proxy. Turn off \"Full DHT on while charging\" to keep the proxy on the charger.
Held off by the connection watcher after a wedge that implicated the proxy — the search-bar hexagon still says proxy. It returns on its own.

Connection mode: by default every account runs on the full distributed DHT — the most robust mode, with no single proxy link that can wedge. On a network that blocks UDP the watcher pins the DHT proxy ON instead, so TURN relays carry traffic until UDP returns. Every check and recovery is recorded in the history, and a full copy is written to files/recovery-log.txt.

Modes cost the same: on a phone that is not recovering in a loop, DHT proxy and full DHT move almost identical amounts — 24.6 vs 24.8 MiB/h measured on a one-account phone, and roughly 25–40 MiB/h per account either way. Pick the mode for reachability, not to save data.

What a recovery costs: turning the proxy off and on again destroys every proxy connection, and the rebuilt one must subscribe from scratch — the server answers a fresh subscription with the FULL contents of every key it watches. One old account key measured 1.29 MiB per subscription, times four accounts, six times in two hours. So recovery no longer touches the proxy unless the proxy itself is the suspect; it re-registers and re-arms presence instead.

Why an old account costs more: the oldest account\'s key still carries about 990 revocation lists published in 2024–2025. They were stored as permanent and unsigned, so nothing — not even this app — can delete or overwrite them, and the proxy ignores any filter a client asks for, so they are sent in full on every fresh subscription. They fade only as the machines holding them restart. A fresh account carries none of this: that is the whole difference between two phones on the same Wi-Fi.
Measuring it yourself: the Data pill at the top of this dashboard runs a live measurement (start, stop, save) and holds both logs — your saved sessions and the automatic hourly record.
Data (top of the dashboard) — live data measurement plus the usage logs. The same meter is on the Connection monitor page.
